summary: I designed one first-round exploration of a WeMod game discovery page, direction "Spotlight": search first, set beside a wall of real game art, then a Top games picker that shows each game's cheat count and links to its page, a section explaining that every game page lists its mods by group, a browse shelf with an A–Z list, and three how-it-works steps that end on the download. On desktop (Windows) the download sits beside the search and again in step 1. On phone (not Windows) there is no download anywhere: the page ends with "...or visit us on your PC to download the app" and a "Browse all games" button. An independent AI review rejected this round (product 58, visual 59), so treat it as a starting point for a second round, not a design to take forward.
limitations: Independent AI review (renders only): Product 58/100, Visual 59/100, status Reject; the reviewer's alignment pass was not run (follow-up message blocked by the guard). Readiness: Blocked.

Top fixes for round 2: a stronger desktop download path, show real mods beside a game (only RDR2 has verified mod names, and its media are not approved), stop repeating the same games across sections, and replace the table-like top-games rows and the empty step cards.
SEO: a new H1 and crawlable game links on a game-list page carry seo_risk high and need Growth sign-off; the metric owner is unknown and no traffic, search or device data was used.
Search, the art wall and the top-games picker are Proposed or provisional patterns: there is no production game-list page save (R93), and the brand-page phone action is undecided (R115).
Placing "WeMod by Wand" above the footer is a decision for the design owner; the brief's request to post to Linear and ask for review is left to the bridge.
Only one of three written narratives was built; the canvas check passed with layout hints (dead zones; HomeSection measured 1024 against the 960 the check expects).
